title: Quantum Information Analysis in a q-Deformed Deng-Fan Model
authors: P. O. Amadi, Collins O. Edet, A. R. P. Moreirae, P. Kalasuwana, N. Ali, R. Endut, S. A. Aljunid
abstract: We introduce a $q$-deformed Deng-Fan potential ($q$DFP) model that enables controlled modulation of short-range repulsion and long-range attraction while preserving the equilibrium configuration. The model is solved exactly within the framework of the time-independent Schrödinger equation, yielding closed-form expressions for the energy eigenvalues and wave functions in terms of hypergeometric functions. We show that the deformation parameter $q$ induces non-uniform spectral shifts and a redistribution of bound states. In particular, for $q<1$, the system exhibits spectral compression and enhanced spatial localization. In addition, we investigate the system from an information-theoretic perspective using Shannon entropy, Fisher information, and Fisher--Shannon complexity measures in both position and momentum spaces. The results reveal that the deformation parameter governs the redistribution of quantum information, establishing a direct connection between spatial confinement and momentum delocalization in accordance with the Białynicki-Birula and Mycielski entropic uncertainty principle. Stronger deformation pushes the quantum state further from the minimum-uncertainty configuration, increasing the entropic excess above the BBM bound and reducing the information content about complementary observables, even as position-space localization sharpens. The analysis of entropic and Fisher information densities further shows how the deformation reshapes both the local information content and the structural complexity of the quantum states. We show that in the limit $q\to 1$, the $q$DFP model is reduced to the standard Deng-Fan potential.
summary: This paper analyzes the $q$-deformed Deng-Fan Potential model to study how parameter deformation affects quantum states in molecular systems. By applying advanced information measures like Shannon and Fisher entropy, the authors show that changing the deformation parameter causes a controlled redistribution of quantum information between position and momentum spaces. This establishes a quantitative link between spatial confinement and informational uncertainty.
main_problem: The study investigates how introducing a deformation parameter ($q$) into the Deng-Fan potential modifies the quantum mechanical energy spectrum and, critically, redistributes the inherent quantum information content of the system.
main_result: Stronger deformation (smaller $q$) enhances spatial localization while simultaneously increasing the entropic excess above the minimum uncertainty bound, demonstrating a complex trade-off in quantum information flow.
method: The authors solve the time-independent Schrödinger equation exactly using hypergeometric functions and analyze the resulting wavefunctions using advanced information-theoretic measures like Shannon entropy and Fisher information.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the $q$-deformed Deng-Fan Potential ($qDFP$), a modification of an empirical potential used in molecular physics to describe diatomic interactions. The Hamiltonian is solved analytically, yielding closed-form solutions for eigenvalues and wavefunctions.
key_observables: Energy eigenvalues ($E_{n,q}$), Shannon entropy ($S_x, S_p$), Fisher information ($I_x, I_p$), and the entropic excess above the BBM bound.
important_parameters: The deformation parameter $q \in (0, 1]$, the potential depth $D_e$, and the equilibrium bond length $x_e$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the system remains physically admissible for $q<1$ and relies on the mathematical framework connecting quantum mechanics to information theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the potential shape change with $q$, show ground state localization sharpening, demonstrate excited state probability density asymmetry, and visualize the concentration shifts of entropic densities in position space.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the $qDFP$ model and solves the Schrödinger equation exactly. It then analyzes the spectral consequences of varying $q$. Finally, it delves into information theory, applying entropy measures to quantify how the deformation reshapes quantum state structure beyond simple energy analysis.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges molecular physics (potential modeling) with fundamental concepts from quantum information theory. The explicit quantification of information trade-offs provides a deeper physical insight into confinement effects than spectral analysis alone.
